rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 7 (kd 0.15) scored 57.61, below the 75.97 baseline. The s-bend progress fell from 0.29 to 0.155, which is below the 0.22 threshold in the Evaluator's rule (2). So kd 0.15 costs progress, and kd returns to 0.2, the value that held progress in iterations 1 and 6. Lowering kd further is ruled out. Across the runs, kd 0.1 and 0.15 both cut s-bend progress to about 0.15, while kd 0.2 gives about 0.29. Every lever tested except base_speed has now been ruled out for max_error. kp 2.5 (iteration 3) left max_error at 0.062 to 0.065. Sensor spacing and footprint changes (iterations 4 and 5) cut progress without moving it. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 for every allowed body_width, so geometry cannot widen it. max_error therefore appears to be set by bend reach and dynamic lag, not gain.

Change. The design is the iteration 1 and 6 baseline (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, ki 0, last_direction, weights -2..2, sensors at x -0.02..0.02, y 0.04, sensor_size 0.012, geometry unchanged) with one lever changed: base_speed 1.4 to 1.5. Iteration 2 lowered speed to 1.2, but it also set kd to 0.1, which we now know cuts progress alone. So the speed effect was never isolated, and raising speed is the untested lever the Evaluator asked for.

Expected result. s-bend progress stays at or near 0.29 and completion_time improves if the run finishes. max_error stays near 0.06 to 0.065, and steering_oscillation stays near 0.23 on the s-bend. The risk is that a faster robot leaves the line on the tightest bend sooner, so progress could fall below 0.29; if it does, base_speed returns to 1.4.

Hypotheses. (H1) Speed 1.5 keeps s-bend progress at or above 0.29, because the kd 0.2 damping holds the line. (H2) If progress falls, speed is a limit on the tightest bend, and the baseline 1.4 stays. (H3) max_error remains about 0.06 to 0.065 whatever the speed, since gain and speed have not moved it.

Measurements wanted: progress, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track (especially s-bend and slalom), max_error and where it peaks, and completion_time if any run finishes.
